meta.title: Checkout outage of 3 November, explained
meta.summary: Checkout failed for 41 minutes after a cache change. This fixture exercises every v2 chapter and all nine visual kinds; the incident is fictional.

context.problem: Without a size limit on cached carts, one huge cart filled the cache node and every checkout timed out because the session lookup waited on it.
goals: A cart over the limit gets a clear error
context.background: The cache was shared by sessions and carts since the 2024 rewrite.

timeline.label: Cart writes start to slow
timeline.detail: p99 write time goes from 4 ms to 900 ms.

timeline.label: AbstractCartSerializationCoordinatorFactory found holding the lock
timeline.detail: A long token on purpose, to check wrapping.

timeline.label: Review: carts and sessions need separate caches

diff.summary: Rejects carts over 256 KB before they reach the cache.
One constant for the cart size limit, read from config.
Sessions get their own cache client.
The shared cart cache wrapper is gone.
How to evict one cart by hand.

options.title: Cap cart size
cons: Very large B2B carts need another path
options.why: It removes the failure mode in one release; splitting caches is the longer fix and is planned.

options.title: Split the caches
options.summary: Sessions and carts on separate nodes.

options.title: Do nothing
options.summary: Rely on alerts and manual eviction.
cons: 41 minutes of lost sales each time

risks.mitigation: Sales ops can raise the limit per account.

risks.risk: The limit is set too low by mistake
risks.mitigation: A dashboard shows refused carts per hour, alerting above 5.
The runbook links to the constant.

rollout.label: Ship the limit behind a flag
Turn it on for 10 percent
rollout.detail: Watch refused carts for a day.

concepts.title: Noisy neighbours
concepts.body: Without isolation, one tenant's load slows every other tenant because they share one resource.

parts.label: Shares one resource
parts.detail: Sessions and carts used one cache node.

parts.label: Everyone waits
parts.detail: Session reads queue behind the write.

visual.title: Where checkouts were lost
visual.caption: Most visitors who reached payment were lost at the session lookup.

concepts.title: Limits are contracts
concepts.body: A limit tells callers what will be refused, so a refusal is an answer, not an outage.

concepts.title: Separate what fails together
concepts.body: Things that must not fail together should not share a resource.

diagrams.title: Where the limit sits
diagrams.caption: The size check runs before the cache, so a huge cart never reaches it.

diagrams.title: The review loop
diagrams.caption: Every incident feeds a fix that is then watched for the next one.

diagrams.title: A cart's states
diagrams.caption: A cart over the limit is refused and never reaches the cache.

diagrams.title: Fixes against goals
diagrams.caption: Only the cap meets every goal this quarter.

diagrams.title: Who owns what
diagrams.caption: Checkout owns the limit, Platform owns both caches.

diagrams.title: What moved
diagrams.caption: Carts and sessions stop sharing a cache, and a cart has a size limit.
notes: The cache split comes next quarter.

diagrams.title: Effort against impact
diagrams.caption: The cap is cheap and removes most of the risk.

diagrams.title: What shares the cache
diagrams.caption: Only the cart writes are both large and on the shared node.

quiz.question: A cart of 300 KB arrives. What does the user see?
quiz.explain: The limit refuses it before the cache. A timeout was the old behaviour.

quiz.question: Which part would you change to raise the limit?
quiz.explain: The constant lives there. cache.ts only holds the client.

quiz.question: Why split the caches later?
options: So one tenant cannot starve another
quiz.explain: Isolation removes the shared failure. It costs more, not less.
